name: Ahimaaz
overview: Ahimaaz is a male biblical figure recognized primarily as the father of Ahinoam, as recorded in 1 Samuel 14:50. Beyond this paternal relationship, there is no additional information about his tribe or other distinguishing attributes in Scripture. His mention is brief but establishes a familial link within the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahimaaz means '[my] brother is fury,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a vivid meaning. This name was not given directly by God but is recorded in 1 Samuel 14:50. No additional titles or names are associated with him in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ahimaaz as the father of Ahinoam, as noted in 1 Samuel 14:50. There are no other documented family relationships or connections provided for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ahimaaz's significance lies in his role as the father of Ahinoam, linking him to the genealogical and familial context within the biblical narrative. Though brief, this connection contributes to the understanding of lineage and heritage in the historical setting of 1 Samuel. His mention underscores the importance of family ties in the unfolding story of Israel.
